9_part_d_iso_capacity_rerun.explanation: This is NOT a regression in the fix. t_write_clock_path (this fix's actual target) improved substantially at all three points: 8.968e-11->4.183e-11 (-53.4%) at N=4, 1.123e-10->5.353e-11 (-52.3%) at N=32, 2.365e-10->9.388e-11 (-60.3%) at N=512. But t_critical = max(t_write_data_setup, t_write_clock_path, t_read_access, t_read_addr_path), and BEFORE this fix, t_write_clock_path was the binding term at N=4 and N=32 (only N=512 was already read-bound, at t_read_addr_path=3.489e-10, since the untapered EnableBuf fix had already pushed its own write path below that floor). After tapering, t_write_clock_path fell below the read-path term at ALL THREE points, so t_critical is now capped by t_read_access/t_read_addr_path everywhere in this specific 3-point comparison -- a completely different mechanism (the Mux binary-select tree's own depth, a function of N only, never touched by either this fix or the previous EnableBuf-replacement fix). The t_critical ratio widening from 3.89x to 7.60x is therefore the READ path's own N-dependence becoming fully visible for the first time in this comparison, now that the write path has been improved enough to stop masking it -- not evidence that clock-path tapering made anything slower. The write-clock-path improvement is real and large; it simply stopped being what Part D's t_critical metric measures, at these specific three points, once it succeeded enough to fall out of the critical path.

supplementary_note_beyond_required_sweep.description: Item 2's required sweep set is {0,2,3,4,6,8}. Probed beyond it at (512,256) out of thoroughness: EF=12/16 give 9.057e-11 (WORSE than EF=8's 8.801e-11, same 3-stage count as EF=8 but a tighter per-stage taper budget), EF=32 gives 8.565e-11 (better again, drops to 2 stages). The minimum within the required set lands at the top of the tested range (EF=8) at the three larger points rather than settling at 3-5 as anticipated -- and the true unconstrained optimum is not monotonic beyond EF=8, because EnableFanout simultaneously sets BOTH stage count (fewer stages for larger EF) AND the per-stage taper ratio (tighter budget for larger EF), and these two effects trade off non-monotonically once stage count stops changing between adjacent EF values.
